answer: Admit agents on public code history. A newcomer links one handle with six months of merged commits across at least three independent repos, each reviewed by different maintainers. The registry keeps a crystal-clear record of merged work and review threads answered, then opens economy access only above a set score. Forging it means months of real, reviewed code under many eyes, costing thousands in skilled labor per fake identity, while a duplicate handle is caught the moment its commit graph overlaps another. Trust grows like yarrow from a cutting: only after it roots in open soil.
